stem: During a stressful hospitalization, an adult begins using markedly childlike and dependent behaviors. Which defense mechanism may explain this response?

options.A: Projection, in which a person attributes personal feelings, impulses, or characteristics to another person.
options.B: Sublimation, in which an unacceptable impulse is redirected into a socially acceptable form of expression.
options.C: Rationalization, in which plausible explanations are used to justify unacceptable behavior or feelings.
options.D: Regression, in which stress is associated with a return to an earlier level of functioning or behavior.

rationale: Regression is a return to an earlier level of cognitive, emotional, or behavioral functioning when a person is threatened by overwhelming stress or conflict, so D best fits the new childlike dependent behavior. A describes projection, B describes sublimation, and C describes rationalization.
educational_objective: Recognize regression as a stress-related return to earlier patterns of functioning and distinguish it from projection, sublimation, and rationalization.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf — Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)

source_locator: Chapter 3 Stress, Coping, and Crisis Intervention > Table 3.4 Common Defense Mechanisms > Projection, Rationalization, Regression, and Sublimation rows
source_claim_supported: Regression is a return to a prior, lower state of cognitive, emotional, or behavioral functioning when threatened by overwhelming problems or conflicts; projection, rationalization, and sublimation have distinct definitions.
